literal: Being one who has humility and one who speaks sweet words is the ornament to a person; other things are not.
translation: Humility and pleasant words are the only true ornaments for a person; all other external adornments are not real ornaments.
modern: ஒருவனுக்குப் பணிவு உடையவனாகவும் இனிய சொற்களைப் பேசுபவனாகவும் விளங்குவதே உண்மையான அணிகலனாகும்; மற்றவை எல்லாம் உண்மையான அணிகலன்கள் அல்ல.
explanation: This couplet defines what constitutes true ornamentation for a human being. The author states that possessing humility and speaking sweet, gentle words are the only genuine ornaments a person can wear. External decorations, such as jewels or fine clothing, are dismissed as not being true ornaments. The inner virtues of character and speech are elevated above physical adornments, emphasizing that moral beauty is far superior to material display.
